subject: Post-call: Pathfinder perf qualification + next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Alice Park <alice@pathfinder.ai>, Charlie Nguyen <charlie@pathfinder.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Pathfinder perf qualification + next steps

Hi Alice / Charlie — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we can qualify performance and cost tradeoffs for your realtime summarization use case.

Summary of Pathfinder goals (as discussed):
- Target UX: streaming transcript -> live summary snippets (token-level streaming) shown to agents in ~2–3s for first summary tokens, incremental updates after.
- Target p95 latency for non-streaming summary API: <= 300ms from request to first token for single-turn requests.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 requests/sec, with concurrency spikes up to 400 concurrent open streaming sessions during peak campaigns.
- Typical average prompt size: ~120 tokens input, expected generated tokens ~60 on average (burst up to 200).

Immediate qualification asks (we need these to size a pilot and provide cost estimates):
1) Confirm what proportion of calls must be streaming vs single-shot (your estimate today was ~60% streaming).
2) Typical session duration (minutes) for streaming sessions; are most sessions short (<=2min) or long (10–30min)?
3) Any regulatory constraints (PII retention windows) that affect caching or KV reuse?
4) Your desired SLA for availability and max tolerated fallback behavior (e.g., degrade to best-effort non-streaming if capacity constrained).

Our initial mitigation & cost levers overview (we’ll provide a formal pilot proposal once we have answers above):
- Continuous batching + micro-batching: reduces per-token cost for small generation workloads while preserving p95 latency via adaptive batch timeouts (we can target <20ms micro-batch windows for low-latency paths).
- Prefix / KV caching: cache warm prefixes for common prompt templates (estimated 10–30% token saving depending on templating).
- Model variants + automated fallbacks: route low-latency traffic to quantized 13B variants for sub-200ms p95, with higher-quality 70B reserved for long-running or heavy-context sessions.
- Quantization profiles: int8 or int4 production-friendly profiles for cost savings; we’ll provide accuracy/quality delta estimates based on your eval set.
- Dedicated pools for streaming hot-paths: ensure concurrency SLOs by isolating pools to avoid noisy neighbor latency spikes.

Next proposed steps:
- Alice/Charlie: provide session-duration distribution and streaming proportion by EOD Thu (5/27).
- Redwood (Marcus + Kim): provide an initial pilot cost estimate and an ops runbook that outlines batching/caching/quant profiles by Fri (5/28).
- Schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive to map telemetry and canary rollout plan — proposed Tue 5/31 at 10:00 PT.

I’ve attached a lightweight SLO worksheet and a sample API call set to help with estimations.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor

Thanks Grace — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers inline: 

- Streaming proportion: ~60% of live agent sessions will use streaming (real-time snippets). The other ~40% are batched background summarizations.
- Session durations: median 3.5 minutes, 75th percentile ~9 minutes, top 5% can be 20–25 minutes (these are rare).
- Regulatory/PII: we retain transcripts for 30 days; short-term caching for inference is acceptable but anything persisted longer than 24 hours needs encryption-at-rest and audit logs.
- SLA expectations: we need 99.9% availability for the live agent path; acceptable fallback is returning a non-streaming summary within 5s for degraded calls.

We can get you a small sample of production calls (anonymized) — I'll share via the Drive link and flag the file with example traffic patterns.

Alice

Thanks Alice — that clarity helps. A few technical points / assumptions for Redwood's pilot sizing (please confirm):

Assumptions we used for initial sizing:
- 200 sustained RPS, 400 peak concurrent streaming sessions.
- Avg input tokens: 120; avg output tokens: 60; avg token generation time at 13B quantized path ~0.8ms/token on target infra; 70B float path ~2.5ms/token.
- Streaming path keeps a small KV context (<=4k tokens) per session; longer contexts will increase memory and reduce batching effectiveness.

Recommended pilot config (high-level):
1) Dedicated hot pool for streaming (N1 nodes, autoscale with concurrency threshold) to keep p95 first-byte streaming <= 2.5s and tail token latency below 150ms.
2) Continuous micro-batching for non-streaming and low-latency short requests (20–30ms batching window) to amortize kernel overhead and reduce cost by ~15–25% depending on utilization.
3) Prefix caching for common prompt templates — we’ll instrument cache-hit telemetry in the pilot and expect 8–20% token savings in the first month.
4) Quant profiles we recommend testing initially: int8-fast (minimal quality impact) and int4-aggressive (cost-savvy, test-only on non-critical traffic).
5) Routing policy: low-latency sessions -> 13B-int8; high-quality / post-call batch -> 70B (or 13B with higher temperature). Fallback: if hot pool saturates, redirect to degraded non-streamed path with a 5s SLA.

Open technical asks for your infra/privacy team:
- Can we deploy a short-lived cache with 24h retention and KMS-managed keys?
- Are there any streaming transport constraints (websocket vs SSE) we should prioritize?

We’ll build a cost model for the pilot showing estimated per-1M requests spend across three scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic). We’ll attach that to the pilot proposal on Fri.

– Marcus

Grace / Marcus — good plan. Confirming the action items from our side: 
- We'll deliver anonymized sample traffic (session-level) and the annotated templates for caching by EOD 5/27 — shared in the Drive link you provided.
- We can support 24h short-lived cache with KMS keys; I'll loop our security lead on the onboarding call.
- Websocket preferred for streaming (bi-directional), SSE acceptable as fallback.

One clarification on fallback behavior: if the hot pool is saturated, we'd prefer a fast degraded stream (reduced token rate) instead of switching immediately to non-streamed full summaries. Is that possible? Also please include a short failure-mode diagram in the pilot runbook so our SRE can evaluate impact.

Happy to join the 5/31 deep-dive — next step: Marcus to send pilot cost/runbook; Grace to schedule the 30-min slot.
